angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 1,020,357 km at 15.60 pc = 0.87 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 64.0853 +/- 0.0904 mas (same row, RUWE 0.86): 15.60 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.467 (1.437 to 1.496) from Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26; astrophysical_parameters of the same source): 1,020,357 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.970 (0.930 to 1.010) from Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26; astrophysical_parameters of the same source); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5591 +/- 1.4 K from Andrae et al. (2023), A&A 674, A27 (Gaia DR3 GSP-Phot), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 5945941905576552064: teff_gspphot 5590.9136 K (16th-84th percentiles 5589.6675-5592.4976), the temperature FLAME used (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202243462). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Andrae et al. (2023), A&A 674, A27 (Gaia DR3 GSP-Phot), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 5945941905576552064: teff_gspphot 5590.9136 K (16th-84th percentiles 5589.6675-5592.4976), the temperature FLAME used (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202243462)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/cervantes.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.092, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 160691 (pscomppars): spectral type G3 IV-V, from Benedict et al. 2022 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163..295B/abstract)
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 160691 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.28 dex, from Benedict et al. 2022 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163..295B/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 160691 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units 0.27848, from Gozdziewski et al. 2007 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2007ApJ...657..546G/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 160691 (pscomppars): age 5.7 Gyr, from Benedict et al. 2022 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163..295B/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: VizieR J/A+A/684/A28/tablea1 (Evolution of lithium in FGK dwarfs), column Prot: 14.04 d, the row 0.0 arcsec from the star's J2000 place. The middle of 3 catalogued periods, 2 of them within 20% of it

spinInclinationSource: Computed here from this record's rotation period, projected rotation speed and radius (1.467 solar radii): sin i = v sin i × P / (2πR) = 0.587. Not a measurement of the axis: the three numbers come from different papers.

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
